title: operator-show-reaches-all-inbox-items
intention: cairn operator show <slug> should find the item regardless of whether it is a pending artifact, an idea, a ticket, or a question — everything the inbox lists should be viewable through the same command.
why: The inbox lists ideas by slug (e.g. 2026-08-30-a-device-that-knows-what-s-important), making them look like they should be viewable with cairn operator show artifact <slug>. But show artifact only searches pending_reviews() berths. The user gets 'no pending artifact matches' for an item the inbox just showed them. The inbox wrote a check the CLI cannot cash.
traces_to: Law 7 — errors are loud at diagnostic surfaces. The error message says 'no match' when the item exists in a different lane; a loud error would say 'not an artifact — found as idea: <path>'.
Akien 2026-09-01: tried cairn operator show artifact a-device-that-knows-what-s-important, got 'no pending artifact matches', filed as a bug.

falsifier.proves_green: cairn operator show <slug> resolves against all inbox item types — artifacts (berths), ideas, tickets, questions — and displays the content. A slug that matches an idea shows the idea. A slug that matches nothing says so across all lanes, not just one.
falsifier.proves_red: RED if: (1) the command still only searches berths; (2) an idea slug returns 'no match' when the idea file exists; (3) the lookup silently picks one lane when the slug matches in multiple (ambiguity must be announced).
falsifier.horizon: Small build — extend show_artifact (or add show_item) in operator_inbox/inbox.py to fall through ideas, tickets, questions when berths don't match.

decisions.text: WHAT resolve() WALKS. resolve(token, **kw) calls gather_all(**kw) — the SAME dict the inbox renders from (lanes: troubles, email, adjudications, lap, questions, design, tickets, intentions, ideas) — then adds three REFERENCE lanes from _reference_lanes(**kw): tickets_done = read_done_tickets(tickets_dir=...), ideas_all = read_all_ideas(ideas_dir=...) (every *.json under ideas/ except _-prefixed, moved-on included), troubles_all = read_all_troubles(path=...) (TroubleDevice(path).all(), CLEARED included). Reference lanes exist because a record that LEFT the inbox (a PROVED ticket, an idea a ticket cites, a cleared trouble) is still on disk and still viewable by id — proves_red clause (2). The kw keys are the fixture roots the existing proof already uses: ideas_dir, questions_dir, troubles_dir, intentions_dir, tickets_dir, firings_root, adjudications_dir; with no kw the live commons is read.

decisions.text: HOW A TOKEN MATCHES — _match_grade(token, ident, title) returns _EXACT (0) when fold(ident) == token; _PREFIX (1) when the token is hex-ish (_HEXISH = ^(open-)?[0-9a-f]{4,}$) and ident.startswith(token) — so 'open-0123' names open-0123456789ab but 'loop' does NOT name loop-not-beating; _LOOSE (2) when ident.endswith('-' + token) (an idea's date-stripped tail: 'a-lot-of-things-look-alike' names 2026-01-01-a-lot-of-things-look-alike) or _slugify(token) equals _slugify(ident) or _slugify(title); None otherwise. resolve() keeps only the hits at the BEST (lowest) grade, so 'c691e19d5464' returns the ticket alone and not the trouble boat-crossed-to-proved-uncovered-c691e19d5464 whose slug merely ends in the id. A candidate listed in both an open lane and a reference lane is counted once, under the open lane (a seen-set on fold(ident)).

decisions.text: HOW AMBIGUITY IS ANNOUNCED — proves_red clause (3). Within one grade every hit is returned; show_item() renders two or more as: first line 'ambiguous — N match <token!r>:' then one line per hit '  [<lane>] <id>  <path>'. resolve() never picks. Zero hits renders: 'no pending artifact, ticket, idea, question, trouble, intention or adjudication matches <token!r> — searched lanes: <comma-joined lanes_searched(**kw)>'. lanes_searched(**kw) = list(gather_all(**kw)) + list(_reference_lanes(**kw)), i.e. the very lanes resolve walked, read off the same dicts.

decisions.text: HOW ONE HIT RENDERS. show_item(): a ticket lane (lane startswith 'tickets') renders via the existing _format_ticket(); adjudications via _format_artifact(); every other lane prints a header '[<lane>] <id>' and 'path: <path>' inside the ===== rules, then the file's JSON pretty-printed (json.dumps indent=2) when the path is a .json, the file text for .md, else the in-memory record. The path is item['source'] or item['path'] when the lane's reader carries one, else _LANE_FILES[<lane prefix>](kw) -> (dir, ext) joined as <dir>/<id><ext>; _LANE_FILES covers ideas (.json), questions (.json), lap (.json), intentions (.md), troubles (.json).

decisions.text: THE VERB AND ITS EXIT CODES. In main(), 'show' with a target that is not 'artifact', 'usage' or one of the existing section names now runs: result = show_item(args[1]); print(result); return 0 if not (result.startswith('no pending artifact') or result.startswith('ambiguous')) else 1. So cairn operator show <slug|id> exits 0 with the record, 1 on no match (naming the lanes searched) and 1 on ambiguity (naming every hit) — a refusal is never a quiet exit 0. show_artifact()'s last line, which used to return 'no pending artifact or ticket matches ...', now returns show_item(id_prefix), so cairn operator show artifact <id> falls through to the same resolver. USAGE gained the line: show <slug|id>          any item the inbox lists — idea, question, trouble, ticket, intention, adjudication, artifact — by the id or slug it printed; exits 1 when nothing (or more than one thing) matches.

decisions.text: Done tickets need no new mechanism and read_done_tickets is NOT new — it already exists in cairn/tools/operator_inbox/inbox.py (def read_done_tickets(*, tickets_dir=None), the reader the inbox's own 'done' section uses). A done ticket is one whose cursor label's leading state (r['label'].split(':')[0], read off workflow_and_state by _scan_tickets, the one walk of tickets/) is in TERMINAL_STATES — imported into inbox.py by 'from cairn.tools.base.transitions import (... TERMINAL_STATES ...)', measured value frozenset({'ABSORBED', 'DROPPED', 'KILLED', 'PROVED', 'RETIRED', 'SUPERSEDED'}) — no status field, no tickets_done/ directory, no index: the same tickets/ files, filtered by terminal cursor. resolve() simply calls the existing read_done_tickets(tickets_dir=kw.get('tickets_dir')) as the tickets_done reference lane. (Corrected in place 2026-09-17: the first writing named four wrong state names; the artifact journal carries the edit.)

fold is the case-fold from cairn.tools.system_word, already imported at the top of inbox.py by 'from cairn.tools.system_word import fold, is_word' (ruled 2026-09-07: any word Akien could type compares through system_word). fold(s) lower-cases and strips a system word so that 'SHOW', 'Show' and 'show' compare equal; _match_grade applies fold to both the token and the candidate id before comparing, and nothing else — free text (titles, prose) is never folded, only slugified via _slugify.

_format_ticket(record_or_doc) and _format_artifact(finding) both pre-exist in cairn/tools/operator_inbox/inbox.py — they are the renderers show_artifact() already used for a ticket and a pending berth respectively (grep -n 'def _format_ticket\|def _format_artifact' cairn/tools/operator_inbox/inbox.py finds both). show_item() reuses them unchanged. The '===== rules' are the existing 76-character '=' separator lines those renderers print above and below a header (the same lines the inbox prints around every section); show_item's own header for a non-ticket lane is: a rule line, '  [<lane>] <id>', '  path: <path>', a rule line, then the body.

read_all_ideas and read_all_troubles are NEW in this build (read_done_tickets is the only pre-existing one of the three). Their code, verbatim as landed in inbox.py beside resolve(): def read_all_ideas(*, ideas_dir: Path | None = None) -> dict: d = ideas_dir or IDEAS_DIR; if not d.exists(): return {'count': 0, 'items': []}; items = [{'id': p.stem} for p in sorted(d.glob('*.json')) if not p.stem.startswith('_')]; return {'count': len(items), 'items': items}.  def read_all_troubles(*, path: str | None = None) -> dict: from cairn.devices.trouble.trouble import TroubleDevice; items = TroubleDevice(path).all(); return {'count': len(items), 'items': items}.  Their return shape is the inbox lane shape ({'count', 'items'}), NOT read_done_tickets' ({'records', 'by_label', 'total'}); _lane_items(payload) reads whichever of ('items', 'records', 'open', 'live', 'findings') a lane carries, so resolve() walks both shapes with one loop.

The two edit points in inbox.py, as they stand. main(argv): after 'if is_word(args[0], "show")' it already has 'target = fold(args[1])' and arms for 'artifact' (show_artifact(args[2])), 'usage' (print USAGE) and the section names; the LAST arm, which used to print 'unknown show target' and return 2, is now: result = show_item(args[1]); print(result); return 0 if not (result.startswith('no pending artifact') or result.startswith('ambiguous')) else 1. show_artifact(id_prefix): its body (search pending berths, then tickets by prefix) is unchanged; only its final 'return f"no pending artifact or ticket matches {id_prefix!r}"' became 'return show_item(id_prefix)'. Both are verified by grep -n 'show_item' cairn/tools/operator_inbox/inbox.py.

print_teeth_main comes from cairn.tools.proof_coverage (from cairn.tools.proof_coverage import print_teeth_main) — the same two-line __main__ block the sibling proof cairn/tools/operator_inbox/proofs/test_operator_inbox.py ends with; it runs every test_* function in the file, prints '  ok <name>' per tooth and exits non-zero on a red — the tester's seal reads those printed tooth names, and a proof that prints none seals RED ('zero teeth printed'). proof_binds_its_subject_at_call_time is a proof_coverage sieve that reds a proof importing a build-added name at module level, which is why resolve/show_item/lanes_searched are imported inside each test function. _scratch_commons(root) is DEFINED IN test_show.py itself (the fixture builder described in D7), not in any framework. The monkeypatch is plain attribute assignment on the imported module (inbox.show_item = lambda tok, **kw: saved(tok, **f)) restored in a finally; no pytest fixture is used, so the file runs under both pytest and print_teeth_main.

The exact __main__ block, the last three lines of test_show.py, verbatim:  if __name__ == "__main__":  /  from cairn.tools.proof_coverage import print_teeth_main  /  raise SystemExit(print_teeth_main(__file__)).  And the in-function import pattern, verbatim from tooth 1:  def test_resolve_reaches_every_lane_not_only_berths():  /  from cairn.tools.operator_inbox.inbox import resolve, lanes_searched, show_item  /  with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='a705-scratch-commons-') as td:  /  f = _scratch_commons(Path(td))  /  ... — the module top imports only json, Path and tempfile.

resolve() normalizes the different lane shapes with _lane_items(payload): for key in ('items', 'records', 'open', 'live', 'findings'): if isinstance(payload, dict) and isinstance(payload.get(key), list): return payload[key]; return []. So gather_all's {'count','items'} lanes, read_done_tickets' {'records',...}, read_questions' {'open',...}, read_troubles' {'live',...} and read_adjudications' {'findings',...} all iterate through the one loop: for lane, payload in data.items(): for item in _lane_items(payload): ... ; _item_id(item) then reads a str item, or item['id'] or item['berth_id'].

_scratch_commons(root) — the exact files it writes under the tmp root, each json.dumps'd. ideas/<stem>.json for stem in ('2026-01-01-a-lot-of-things-look-alike', '2026-01-05-ticket-and-task', '2026-01-06-ticket-and-task'): {'prose': stem, 'author': 'Akien'}. questions/open-0123456789ab.json: {'id': 'open-0123456789ab', 'question': 'one question?', 'ticket': 'aaaaaaaaaaaa'}. troubles/boat-stuck-at-buildme.json: {'id': 'boat-stuck-at-buildme', 'standing': 'CLEARED', 'count': 1, 'why': 'a fixture trouble, cleared'}. troubles/loop-not-beating.json: {'id': 'loop-not-beating', 'standing': 'OPEN', 'count': 2, 'why': 'fixture live'}. intentions/I-no-ticket-yet.md: the text '# no ticket yet\n'. tickets/aaaaaaaaaaaa-fixture.json: {'id': 'aaaaaaaaaaaa', 'title': 'fixture ticket', 'linked_ideas': ['2026-01-01-a-lot-of-things-look-alike'], 'workflow_and_state': 'code-seam@v2: THINKME -> [TICKETME] -> BUILDME -> PROVED'}. Also mkdir'd empty: adjudications/ and skill_block_instance/berths/intent/. It returns {'ideas_dir': ideas, 'questions_dir': questions, 'troubles_dir': str(troubles), 'intentions_dir': intentions, 'tickets_dir': tickets, 'firings_root': firings, 'adjudications_dir': lap} — the kw every reader in gather_all accepts. Meaning in the teeth: linked_ideas on the ticket is what makes the 01-01 idea MOVED ON (read_ideas drops an idea a ticket cites); standing CLEARED is what drops the trouble from live(); the two ticket-and-task ideas are the one collision.

COMMONS_ROOT, TICKETS_DIR, IDEAS_DIR, QUESTIONS_DIR, INTENTIONS_DIR and ADJUDICATIONS_DIR are pre-existing module-level constants at lines 25-36 of inbox.py, each Path(os.environ.get('CAIRN_...', <default under CairnCommons>)). There is NO TROUBLES_DIR constant: the trouble lane's default root belongs to TroubleDevice (its __init__ takes root=None and defaults to ~/dev/src/CairnCommons/troubles), which is why _LANE_FILES['troubles'] computes Path(kw['troubles_dir']) if given else COMMONS_ROOT / 'troubles', and read_all_troubles passes kw.get('troubles_dir') straight to TroubleDevice(path).

_reference_lanes(**kw) is a NEW four-line function in this build, verbatim: def _reference_lanes(**kw) -> dict: return {'tickets_done': read_done_tickets(tickets_dir=kw.get('tickets_dir')), 'ideas_all': read_all_ideas(ideas_dir=kw.get('ideas_dir')), 'troubles_all': read_all_troubles(path=kw.get('troubles_dir'))}. It composes the pre-existing read_done_tickets (D10) with the new read_all_ideas and read_all_troubles (D13); resolve() does data = gather_all(**kw); data.update(_reference_lanes(**kw)) and lanes_searched() does list(gather_all(**kw)) + list(_reference_lanes(**kw)).

Signatures, verbatim: def resolve(token: str, **kw) -> list[dict]; def show_item(token: str, **kw) -> str; def lanes_searched(**kw) -> list[str]. kw is Python's ordinary **kwargs (empty dict when nothing is passed) and is forwarded unchanged to gather_all(**kw) and _reference_lanes(**kw); every reader in gather_all takes optional keyword roots defaulting to the live commons constants, so resolve('x') / show_item('x') with no kw read the live commons and resolve('x', **f) reads the scratch roots f. main() calls show_item(args[1]) with no kw.

_LANE_FILES, AS IT STANDS in cairn/tools/operator_inbox/inbox.py (line 835): a module-level dict mapping a lane PREFIX to a callable kw -> (dir, ext): 'ideas' -> (kw.get('ideas_dir') or IDEAS_DIR, '.json'); 'questions' -> (kw.get('questions_dir') or QUESTIONS_DIR, '.json'); 'lap' -> (kw.get('adjudications_dir') or ADJUDICATIONS_DIR, '.json'); 'intentions' -> (kw.get('intentions_dir') or INTENTIONS_DIR, '.md'); 'troubles' -> (Path(kw['troubles_dir']) if kw.get('troubles_dir') else COMMONS_ROOT / 'troubles', '.json'). kw is the same keyword dict show_item was called with, so a proof's fixture dirs override the live ones. The lane PREFIX is lane.split('_')[0] — the payload key up to its first underscore (so 'questions_open' -> 'questions', 'lap_pending' -> 'lap'). Path resolution per hit, in order: item['source'] or item['path'] when the item is a dict carrying either; else, when the prefix is a _LANE_FILES key, Path(dir) / f'{id}{ext}'; else path is None and the listed record itself is rendered.
